description: Concentric double-double ditched square enclosure, primarily dated by pottery to the late 3rd - early 4th CE. No other features were recorded, but a religious interpretation was put forward, and the RSRB marks the site as a 'shrine'. It is noted that an altar was found in the grounds of Elmete hall in the 19th CE but no find spot is known.
bibliography: Martyn, Blick, Brindle, and et al. “Elmete Caravan Park, Roundhay (West Yorkshire).” The Rural Settlement of Roman Britain: an online resource, 2015. https://doi.org/10.5284/1030449.
